hook: A field of grass can feed a herd of grazers, the grazers a few predators, and the predators perhaps one large hunter. Every step up loses most of the energy as heat. That single fact explains why big predators are rare, why there are so few trophic levels, and why eating plants feeds more people per acre than eating meat.

prereq.q: What is the trophic level of a herbivore?
Which setup gives what percent 650 is of 2,500?

options: the energy reaching the top predator

figure.caption: An energy pyramid: about 10% of the energy passes up each level.

chain.cause: Organisms at each level use most of their food energy for respiration and body heat
chain.effect: that energy leaves as heat and cannot be passed on

chain.cause: Some of each level is never eaten, or is lost in waste
chain.effect: that energy goes to decomposers instead

chain.cause: Only about 10% is stored as new tissue
chain.effect: about 10% is available to the next level up, so energy shrinks at every step

ideas: The 10% rule: about 10% of the energy at one trophic level reaches the next. Multiply by 0.10 for each step up.
The first law of thermodynamics: energy is not created or destroyed. The second law: every transfer turns some into heat, so no transfer is 100% efficient.
An energy pyramid always narrows going up; biomass pyramids usually do too.
Transfer efficiency = energy at the higher level ÷ energy at the lower level × 100.

misconception.wrong: Energy is used up or destroyed as it moves up the trophic levels.
misconception.right: Energy is not destroyed (first law). It changes form, and at each step most of it becomes heat released to the surroundings (second law), which organisms cannot use as food.

summary: Energy enters ecosystems through producers and flows one way, up the trophic levels. At each step about 90% is used for life processes and lost as heat, so only about 10% passes on: multiply by 0.10 for each step. This explains energy pyramids, the small number of trophic levels and why eating at a lower level feeds more people. Energy is not destroyed; it leaves as heat.
